messages:
Maria: quick check-in on the phased preemptive cohorting idea i sketched in the RFC — want to make sure we captured the queueing tradeoffs before we lock the API.
Alex: thanks — summary pls? i skimmed, but hard to parse all the failure modes.
Maria: short summary — split tenants into short-lived microlanes and long-lived cohorts. preemption allowed only at epoch boundaries for cohorts to avoid kv-cache thrash. phased rollout means we start with non-preemptive cohorts, observe, then enable soft-preempt for noisy tenants.
Sam: main worry: how do we bound injustice? if a noisy tenant is stuck in cohort for epoch length T, latency tail for others might spike.
Alex: agreed. Two knobs: epoch length and preemption granularity. If epoch length is small we get more churn; if too big we hurt fairness.
Jen: telemetry perspective: we need per-tenant p50/p95 token latency and a headroom metric that captures kv-cache reuse ratio. otherwise we won't see the thrash signal until it's too late.
Maria: action item: add headroom ratio -> hits_on_prefetch / total_prefetch as a signal. threshold triggers soft-preempt.
Sam: soft-preempt = move tenant to micro-lane for N requests, then re-evaluate? what about loss of kv warmup cost estimated as warm_cost = avg_kv_restore_tokens * cost_per_token?
Alex: proposal: soft-preempt duration should be proportional to estimated kv-warm-cost. i.e., duration = clamp(kv_warm_cost / c, min=1s, max=epoch/2). We need safe defaults.
Maria: ❤️ that feels principled. Also want explicit fallback: if micro-lane saturates, route to best-effort model variant (quantized) to keep tail bounded.
Jen: logging: annotate routes with routing.decider=id, cohort_id, preempted=true/false. export as tag for traces so SLO dashboards can filter.
Sam: race conditions: if we preempt mid-batch arrival, we must guarantee we don't drop requests. spec says: preemption = stop new enqueues to cohort lane, let in-flight finish, drain, then move queued requests to micro-lane. any objections?
Alex: fine but draining could cause head-of-line blocking for long-running in-flight. consider selective migration: for queued requests only, not in-flight. handle in-flight with a soft deadline that can be hedged.
Maria: yes — we already discussed hedging short requests < X tokens. maybe we define in-flight hedging policy: if in-flight expected remaining > hedge_threshold, spawn a parallel micro-lane replicate and accept first responder.
Sam: hedging implies extra GPU cost. we should only enable replicate hedging when predicted SLA breach probability > p0. add prediction model hook.
Jen: from metrics side, add flags: routing.replicate=true/false and replicate_cost_est in trace. helps correlate cost-to-latency.
infra-bot: deploy queued: batcher-preemptive-rollout v0.3 -> staging at 2026-03-17T15:22Z 🚀
Alex: noted deploy. we should gate with canary for 10% cohorts, verify headroom signal and kv-reuse across 24h.
Maria: agreed. plan: canary steps: 1) instrument headroom and kv_reuse, 2) enable soft-preempt for 10% cohorts, 3) monitor p99 and cost delta, 4) expand to 50% if stable.
Sam: one more tradeoff: queue length visibility. do we expose per-cohort queue_len metrics? can be high cardinality.
Jen: prefer aggregated percentiles plus a sampled per-cohort queue_len for top-k tenants. store top-k via streaming sketch to avoid cardinality explosion.
Alex: also need API boundaries: users can pin "non-preemptible" for regulatory tenants. default is preemptible. we need clear error codes when preemption would violate pinned policy.
Maria: yes add routing.error = PREEMPTION_BLOCKED for those attempts, with human-friendly reason.
Sam: testing: simulate a noisy tenant with 10x request rate and compare epoch=500ms vs 2s. we should include deterministic unit for admission simulation.
Alex: good. i can add simulator changes to the admission repo.
Jen: small ask — add a dashboard tile showing kv_cache_hit_ratio and cohort_headroom_heatmap. that will make rollouts less nerve-wracking.
Maria: summary of concrete next steps: Alex -> simulator and duration formula, Jen -> telemetry tags + dashboards, Sam -> load tests & cost model, me -> update RFC with preemption state machine + API wording. roll call on timelines?
Alex: simulator PR by EOD Fri.
Sam: load tests start Mon, 48h run, will upload results.
Jen: dashboard mock by Tue morning.
infra-bot: canary rule applied: cohorts 10% selected by hash(mod 10) at 2026-03-18T02:00Z
Maria: perfect. i'll update RFC and ping legal for non-preemptible policy wording. thanks all :thumbsup:
